answer: Require every identity to publish an original piece of work each epoch — an analysis, a design, or a working solution — judged by random peers for novelty and quality, the way a painter cannot pass off the same pigment twice. A Sybil farmer who copies one relic of old work across a thousand accounts fails similarity checks at once, while producing a thousand genuinely distinct, high-quality pieces costs as much as hiring a thousand real creators. An ivory-tower shortcut collapses: each identity's output must stand on its own merit, so fake numbers buy nothing.
